title: RPF Constable & Sub-Inspector (SI) Syllabus 2026: Detailed Topic-Wise Weightage, Physical Standards & Exam Pattern PDF
summary: Everything you need to crack the Railway Protection Force (RPF) Constable and Sub-Inspector recruitments: granular CBT syllabus for Arithmetic, Reasoning, and General Awareness, 1600m running benchmarks, physical criteria (PET/PST), 7th CPC salary, and free mock test portals.
author: Sarkari Aavedan Editorial Team
content:
## Introduction & Service Overview

The Railway Protection Force (**RPF**) and Railway Protection Special Force (**RPSF**) under the Ministry of Railways conduct nationwide centralized recruitment examinations via the Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) for **Constable (Executive)** and **Sub-Inspector (Executive)** positions. Tasked with protecting millions of daily railway passengers, securing railway infrastructure across 68 divisions, and curbing crime in station premises, RPF personnel enjoy prestigious Central Police perks, Ministry of Railways free travel passes (Privilege Pass), uniform allowances, and 7th Central Pay Commission compensation.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> The **1600 Meters Run for RPF Constable (5 mins 45 secs)** is recognized as one of the toughest physical standards among all Indian uniformed services. **Only 1 chance** is given for the run — candidates who fail the running test are disqualified on the spot regardless of how high their written CBT score is!

## RPF Posts & Pay Scales (7th CPC)

| Post Name | Qualification Requirement | 7th CPC Pay Level | Entry Basic Pay | Approx In-Hand Starting Salary (Class X City) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **RPF Sub-Inspector (SI) (Executive)** | Graduate Degree in any stream | **Level-6** | ₹35,400 – ₹1,12,400 | ₹58,000 – ₹65,000 / month (Plus Uniform & Ration Allowance) |
| **RPF Constable (Executive)** | 10th (Matriculation) Passed | **Level-3** | ₹21,700 – ₹69,100 | ₹34,000 – ₹38,000 / month (Plus Free Railway Medical & Travel Pass) |

## Step-by-Step Selection Procedure

1. **Computer Based Test (CBT)**: 120 objective questions for 120 marks in 90 minutes conducted across computerized test centers nationwide.
2. **Physical Efficiency Test (PET) & Physical Measurement Test (PST)**: Candidates qualifying the written cutoff (10 times the vacancy count) appear for biometric verification, height/chest measurement, and endurance running.
3. **Document Verification (DV)**: Scrutiny of original academic certificates, category certificates (OBC-NCL/SC/ST/EWS), and character antecedents.
4. **Railway Medical Fitness Examination**: Strict Railway Medical standard (B-1 standard with minimum 6/9, 6/12 distant vision; color blindness is strictly disqualified).
5. **Basic Training**: 9-month military and legal training at centralized academies like JR RPF Academy Lucknow or RPF Training Center Moula Ali Hyderabad.

## Computer Based Test (CBT) Pattern & Weightage Graph

The written CBT consists of 120 multiple choice questions for 120 marks in 90 minutes. There is **1/3rd negative marking** for every incorrect answer.

| Section / Subject | Questions | Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Core High-Yield Focus Areas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness** | 50 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:41.7%:General Awareness] | Everyday General Science (PCB), Indian History, Art & Culture, Geography, Polity, Current Affairs, Sports |
| **Arithmetic (Mathematics)** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Arithmetic] | Number Systems, Percentages, Ratio & Proportion, Averages, Time & Work, Profit & Loss, Speed Distance Time, SI/CI |
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Reasoning] | Analogies, Series, Coding-Decoding, Blood Relations, Syllogisms, Direction Sense, Non-Verbal Puzzles |
| **Grand Total** | **120 Questions** | **120 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Composite]** | **Composite Time: 90 Minutes (Sectional Cutoff: None)** |

> [!TIP]  
> **The 50-Mark General Awareness Core**: General Awareness accounts for **41.7% of the total paper**! Aspirants who score 38+ in GA and combine it with 30+ in Reasoning routinely secure cutoffs above 90+ out of 120.

## Granular Topic-Wise Syllabus for RPF CBT

### 1. Arithmetic Syllabus (35 Questions / 35 Marks)
- **Number Systems**: Integers, Whole Numbers, Rational Numbers, Divisibility Rules, Prime Factorization.
- **Decimals and Fractions**: VBODMAS order of operations, simplification of nested expressions.
- **Relationships Between Numbers**: Factors, Multiples, LCM and HCF application problems.
- **Fundamental Arithmetical Operations**: Percentages, Ratio & Proportion, Averages.
- **Commercial Mathematics**: Simple Interest and Compound Interest, Profit and Loss, Successive Discounts.
- **Work, Time & Distance**: Time and Work, Work & Wages, Pipes and Cisterns, Relative Speed, Train problems, Boats and Streams.
- **Mensuration**: Areas and perimeters of rectangles, circles, triangles; surface areas and volumes of spheres, cylinders, and cubes.
- **Data Interpretation**: Reading tables, line graphs, and bar charts.

### 2. General Intelligence & Reasoning (35 Questions / 35 Marks)
- **Analogies & Classification**: Semantic, symbolic, and number analogies; odd one out.
- **Spatial Orientation & Visualization**: Mirror images, water images, pattern completion, folding figures.
- **Coding-Decoding**: Direct letter shifting, substitute coding, matrix-based alphanumeric codes.
- **Logical Deduction**: Syllogisms (standard Venn diagrams), Statement-Conclusion, Statement-Argument.
- **Relationship Concepts**: Blood relations (family trees, pointing clues), Direction sense test.
- **Series & Ordering**: Number series, alphabet series, ranking test, seating arrangements (linear & circular).
- **Non-Verbal Reasoning**: Embedded figures, cube & dice rotation, visual series progression.

### 3. General Awareness Syllabus (50 Questions / 50 Marks)
- **General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Life Sciences)**: 10th CBSE NCERT level; Newton's laws, light & optics, chemical equations, acids/bases, human organ systems, vitamins and deficiency diseases.
- **Indian History**: Harappan Civilization, Vedic era, Mauryas, Guptas, Mughal Empire, 1857 revolt, Indian National Congress sessions, Indian Independence movement.
- **Art & Culture**: Classical dances of India (Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, etc.), folk music, regional festivals, UNESCO World Heritage sites in India.
- **Indian Geography**: River systems, mountain ranges, climate zones, soils, national parks, mineral reserves, borders with neighboring countries.
- **Indian Polity & Constitution**: Preamble, Fundamental Rights & Duties, President, Prime Minister, Governor, Supreme Court, Panchayati Raj, Key Constitutional Amendments.
- **Indian Economy & Railways**: 5-year plans, GDP concepts, inflation, RBI monetary policy, Indian Railways history, bullet train corridors, Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFC).
- **Sports & Current Affairs**: Olympic & Paralympic games, Cricket World Cup, Asian Games, major trophies, recent national and international awards, summit meets (G20, BRICS).

## Physical Efficiency Test (PET) — Constable vs. Sub-Inspector

> [!WARNING]  
> For the running events (1600m & 800m), **ONLY ONE CHANCE** is provided. For Long Jump and High Jump events, candidates are given a maximum of **2 chances**.

| Event | RPF Constable (Male) | RPF Constable (Female) | RPF Sub-Inspector (Male) | RPF Sub-Inspector (Female) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1600 Meters Running** | **5 Mins 45 Secs** (1 Chance) | Not Applicable | **6 Mins 30 Secs** (1 Chance) | Not Applicable |
| **800 Meters Running** | Not Applicable | **3 Mins 40 Secs** (1 Chance) | Not Applicable | **4 Mins 00 Secs** (1 Chance) |
| **Long Jump** | **14 Feet** (2 Chances) | **9 Feet** (2 Chances) | **12 Feet** (2 Chances) | **9 Feet** (2 Chances) |
| **High Jump** | **4 Feet** (2 Chances) | **3 Feet** (2 Chances) | **3 Feet 9 Inches** (2 Chances) | **3 Feet** (2 Chances) |

## 12-Week Physical Conditioning & Running Protocol

- **Weeks 1 to 4 (Base Aerobic Conditioning)**: Run 3 to 4 km at an easy conversational pace 5 mornings a week to build cardiovascular endurance. Perform bodyweight squats, lunges, and calf raises.
- **Weeks 5 to 8 (Interval Repeats)**: Shift to 400-meter track intervals (target 80–82 seconds per lap) with 90-second recoveries. Practice landing drills for the Long Jump onto sandpits.
- **Weeks 9 to 12 (Race Simulation)**: Time your 1600m trial on a standard 400m track every Saturday morning. Target 5:35 to create a safety margin on race day.
